banh-canh-cha-ca-quy-nhon.name: Quy Nhon Fish-Cake Soup with Thick Rice Noodles
aliases: Binh Dinh fish-cake soup with thick rice noodles
banh-canh-cha-ca-quy-nhon.serving_basis: Four hot bowls of thick rice-flour noodles, each topped with fried and steamed fish cake.
banh-canh-cha-ca-quy-nhon.description: A Quy Nhon coastal specialty with clear fish-bone broth, tender-chewy thick rice noodles and two kinds of fish cake. This home version uses fresh packaged noodles to simplify the work while keeping the local style of serving it hot with scallions, pepper and chili.
banh-canh-cha-ca-quy-nhon.finished_dish: The broth is clear with a gentle fish aroma; the noodles are soft yet chewy, with sweet steamed fish cake and fragrant fried fish cake.
banh-canh-cha-ca-quy-nhon.serving: Divide the noodles among bowls, ladle over hot broth and arrange the fish cake on top. Finish with scallions, cilantro and fried shallots; serve with lemon and chili.
tips: Choose fresh fish-head bones and remove the gills and clotted blood for a clear, clean-tasting broth.
Cook the noodles separately according to package directions, then portion them into bowls so the broth stays clear.
If making fish cakes from raw fish, steam or fry until the center reaches at least 63°C; use separate boards and plates for raw fish.
dish_type: Fish-cake soup with thick rice noodles
search_terms: Quy Nhon fish-cake soup with thick rice noodles
banh-canh-cha-ca-quy-nhon.image_alt: A bowl of Quy Nhon fish-cake soup with thick rice noodles, steamed and fried fish cakes, scallions and clear broth.
banh-canh-cha-ca-quy-nhon.time_note: About 75 minutes; simmer the fish bones for 35–40 minutes and cook noodles separately to keep the broth clear.

ingredients.name: Sea-fish bones and head
ingredients.notes: Rinse briefly; remove gills and dark blood. Sea bass or other mild fish bones work well.

ingredients.name: Fresh thick rice-flour noodles
ingredients.notes: Use rice-flour or rice-and-wheat noodles; cook separately.

ingredients.name: Cooked steamed fish cake
ingredients.notes: Made from sea fish; slice for serving.

ingredients.name: Cooked fried fish cake
ingredients.notes: Slice for serving; cook fully if using uncooked cake.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Use lightly to balance the broth.

preparation_steps.instruction: Remove the gills, rinse the fish bones and head briefly under cold water, and drain. Wash hands, knife and surfaces after handling raw fish.
Crush the shallots and slice the fish cake. Wash, drain and chop the scallions and cilantro.
Set out the noodles, broth pot and seasonings; keep raw ingredients separate from ready-to-eat greens.

cooking_steps.instruction: Put the fish bones, shallots and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer for 35–40 minutes. Strain out the bones and keep the broth hot.
Season the broth with fish sauce, salt and sugar. Cook the thick rice-flour noodles separately until tender according to the noodle type; drain and divide among four bowls.

Add both kinds of fish cake to the broth and simmer gently for 3–4 minutes until piping hot. Ladle over the noodles, garnish with scallions, cilantro, fried shallots and pepper, and serve with chili and lemon.

banh-canh-cha-ca-quy-nhon.media_alt_text: A bowl of Quy Nhon thick rice-flour noodles with tender noodles, steamed and fried fish cakes, scallions and clear broth.

muc-mot-nang-nuong-muoi-ot-phan-thiet.name: Phan Thiet One-Sun-Dried Squid Grilled with Chili Salt
muc-mot-nang-nuong-muoi-ot-phan-thiet.serving_basis: One platter of grilled one-sun-dried squid to share among four people, with rice or greens.
muc-mot-nang-nuong-muoi-ot-phan-thiet.description: Phan Thiet squid is dried in the sun once, so its surface is dry while the flesh stays supple and sweet. A quick chili-salt grill brings out its seaside flavor; this version balances the seasoning for a family meal.
muc-mot-nang-nuong-muoi-ot-phan-thiet.finished_dish: The squid is firm, lightly charred and fragrant, opaque and tender inside; a thin layer of chili salt seasons without hiding its flavor.
muc-mot-nang-nuong-muoi-ot-phan-thiet.serving: Cut the squid on a diagonal and serve with lime and herbs. Eat hot with steamed rice or wrap in rice paper with greens.
tips: Choose one-sun squid from a traceable source and keep it chilled; thaw frozen squid overnight in the refrigerator.
Pat the squid dry before grilling to reduce splatter and help it brown evenly.
Grill until the thickest part is opaque and reaches 63°C; never reuse the plate that held raw squid.
search_terms: Phan Thiet one-sun squid grilled with chili salt
muc-mot-nang-nuong-muoi-ot-phan-thiet.image_alt: Phan Thiet one-sun-dried squid grilled with chili salt, lightly charred and served with lime.
muc-mot-nang-nuong-muoi-ot-phan-thiet.time_note: About 35 minutes, including a 10-minute marinade; grill briefly on each side to keep the squid tender.

ingredients.name: One-sun-dried cuttlefish
ingredients.notes: Choose supple Phan Thiet squid in sealed packaging and keep it chilled.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use sparingly because the squid is naturally briny.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Finely mince; reduce for less heat.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Mix with the chili salt for a thin coating.

preparation_steps.instruction: If frozen, thaw the squid in the refrigerator. Pat dry, score the thick mantle lightly, and keep tools that touched raw squid separate.
Pound or mince the chili and mix with salt, oil and lime juice into a paste.
Brush a thin layer of seasoning on both sides of the squid and refrigerate for 10 minutes while the grill or grill pan heats.

cooking_steps.instruction: Grill over medium-high heat for about 3–5 minutes per side, depending on thickness, turning once until lightly charred.
Check that the thickest part is opaque and reaches at least 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate and rest for 2 minutes.
Slice diagonally and serve hot with lime, rice or fresh greens for wrapping.

muc-mot-nang-nuong-muoi-ot-phan-thiet.media_alt_text: A plate of Phan Thiet sun-dried squid grilled with chili salt, lightly charred and served with lime.

ghe-luoc-ham-ninh-phu-quoc.name: Ham Ninh Boiled Crab with Lime-Pepper Salt
aliases: Phu Quoc crab with lime-pepper salt
ghe-luoc-ham-ninh-phu-quoc.serving_basis: Four portions of boiled crab, about one medium crab per person.
ghe-luoc-ham-ninh-phu-quoc.description: Ham Ninh crab is prized for its sweet, firm meat. The simple local preparation boils fresh crab and serves it with lime-pepper salt, letting the seafood and fragrant Phu Quoc pepper stand out.
ghe-luoc-ham-ninh-phu-quoc.finished_dish: The shells are bright red and the meat is opaque, firm and sweet; the dipping salt is tangy and peppery without overwhelming the crab.
ghe-luoc-ham-ninh-phu-quoc.serving: Arrange the hot crabs on a large platter with lime-pepper salt and herbs. Crack each crab as you eat and use a separate plate for shells.
tips: Choose live crab with intact shells and keep it chilled; do not cook crab that was dead before cooking.
Scrub the shells and legs under cold running water; keep live crab away from herbs, lime and ready-to-eat food.
Boil until the shell is red and the meat is firm and opaque. Serve on a clean platter and refrigerate leftovers within two hours.
search_terms: Phu Quoc crab with lime pepper salt
ghe-luoc-ham-ninh-phu-quoc.image_alt: A platter of bright red boiled Ham Ninh crab with lime-pepper salt.
ghe-luoc-ham-ninh-phu-quoc.time_note: About 40 minutes; boil a few minutes longer for larger crab until the meat is firm and opaque.

ingredients.name: Live Ham Ninh flower crab
ingredients.notes: About four medium crabs; buy fresh and keep chilled until cooking.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: Juice it and cut extra wedges if desired.

preparation_steps.instruction: Check that the crabs are alive and their shells intact. Scrub the shell, underside and legs under cold running water; wash hands and tools after handling raw crab.
Bring salted water to a boil. Toast the pepper briefly in a dry pan, crush it, and juice the lime.
Mix coarse salt with pepper, lime juice and chili for dipping; keep it away from the raw-crab preparation area.

cooking_steps.instruction: When the water is at a full boil, lower in the crabs with tongs, cover and bring back to a boil.
Boil for about 12–18 minutes depending on size, until evenly red and the meat at a large leg joint is firm and opaque. Open a joint to check.
Transfer to a clean platter, cool briefly and serve with lime-pepper salt. Discard crab that was dead before cooking and refrigerate leftovers within two hours.

ghe-luoc-ham-ninh-phu-quoc.media_alt_text: Freshly boiled red Ham Ninh crabs served with lime-pepper salt.

mat-ca-ngu-tiem-thuoc-bac-phu-yen.name: Phu Yen Tuna Eye Stewed with Chinese Herbs
aliases: Phu Yen tuna eye with Chinese herbs
mat-ca-ngu-tiem-thuoc-bac-phu-yen.serving_basis: Four small bowls of stewed tuna eye, one serving per person.
mat-ca-ngu-tiem-thuoc-bac-phu-yen.description: A Tuy Hoa specialty that uses the large eye from ocean tuna and gently stews it with an edible Chinese-herb soup packet, red dates, goji berries and ginger. The broth is aromatic and the flesh around the eye becomes rich and tender; this home recipe makes four small bowls and makes no medicinal claims.
mat-ca-ngu-tiem-thuoc-bac-phu-yen.finished_dish: The tuna eye is tender but holds its shape, and the clear broth is gently fragrant with ginger and herbs, lightly savory with a sweet finish from the dates.
mat-ca-ngu-tiem-thuoc-bac-phu-yen.serving: Ladle an eye and broth into each warm clay bowl. Serve with perilla, scallions and bread or fresh rice noodles.
tips: Buy cleaned tuna eyes from a reputable seafood supplier, keep chilled and thaw in the refrigerator; discard anything with sour, ammonia-like or spoiled odors.
Use a food-grade herb soup packet with a labeled ingredient list, not an unidentified medicinal mixture.
Stew until the thickest flesh reaches 63°C and is tender; keep the knife, board and plate that touched raw tuna separate.
search_terms: Phu Yen tuna eye stewed with Chinese herbs
mat-ca-ngu-tiem-thuoc-bac-phu-yen.image_alt: A clay pot of Phu Yen tuna eye stewed with Chinese herbs, red dates, goji berries and ginger.
mat-ca-ngu-tiem-thuoc-bac-phu-yen.time_note: About 85 minutes; gently steam for 50–60 minutes until tender and cooked through.

ingredients.name: Cleaned ocean-tuna eyes
ingredients.notes: Buy from a reputable source and keep chilled; thaw in the refrigerator if needed.

ingredients.name: Food-grade Chinese-herb soup packet
ingredients.notes: Choose a food product with a clear ingredient label.

ingredients.name: Dried red dates
ingredients.notes: Rinse briefly; remove pits from large dates.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a little for blanching and seasoning.

preparation_steps.instruction: Thaw tuna eyes in the refrigerator if needed. Check the smell and packaging, pat dry with paper towels, and do not leave raw seafood at room temperature.
Rinse the dates, goji berries and food-grade herb packet. Slice the ginger, crush the shallots and prepare a steamer pot.
Bring 500 ml water to a boil with a few ginger slices and a pinch of salt. Set out four heatproof lidded clay bowls or cups.

cooking_steps.instruction: Blanch the tuna eyes in the boiling ginger water for 1–2 minutes and drain. Divide the eyes, herb packet, dates, goji, shallots and ginger among four heatproof bowls; add 400 ml water.
Set the bowls on a rack above gently simmering water, cover and steam for 50–60 minutes. Add more boiling water to the outer pot if needed.
Check that the thickest flesh reaches at least 63°C and is tender. Season with fish sauce and pepper, garnish with scallions, and serve hot with perilla and bread or noodles.

mat-ca-ngu-tiem-thuoc-bac-phu-yen.media_alt_text: A clay pot of Phu Yen tuna eye stew with red dates, goji berries and ginger.

cha-nhum-phu-quoc.name: Phu Quoc Sea Urchin Patties
aliases: Sea-urchin patties with sesame rice cracker
cha-nhum-phu-quoc.serving_basis: One plate of sea-urchin patties with sesame rice cracker, fresh greens and green banana for four people.
cha-nhum-phu-quoc.description: Cha nhum is a Phu Quoc sea specialty: fresh sea-urchin meat is beaten with scallions, pepper and fish sauce, then fried until golden. This home version forms small patties for easy turning and keeps the traditional sides of thick sesame rice cracker, fresh greens and green banana.
cha-nhum-phu-quoc.finished_dish: The patties are golden and fragrant, set through the center yet softly rich; pepper, scallions and fish sauce bring out the flavor of the sea.
cha-nhum-phu-quoc.serving: Arrange the hot patties on a plate and serve with sesame rice cracker, fresh greens and thinly sliced green banana. Eat as a savory rice-side dish or wrap in rice paper.
tips: Buy cleaned sea-urchin meat from a reputable seafood seller and keep it chilled; thaw in the refrigerator if frozen.
Season fish sauce lightly because the sea-urchin meat is already briny; fry one small test patty before adjusting.
Use a clean pan and plate; fry until the center reaches at least 63°C and do not eat any leftover raw sea-urchin meat.
cha-nhum-phu-quoc.image_alt: Golden Phu Quoc sea-urchin patties with sesame rice cracker, fresh greens and green banana.
cha-nhum-phu-quoc.time_note: About 40 minutes; fry small patties so the centers cook before the outsides brown too deeply.

ingredients.name: Cleaned sea-urchin meat
ingredients.notes: Use fresh or traceably frozen roe from a reputable seafood seller.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust for the natural brininess of the sea urchin.

ingredients.name: Thick sesame rice cracker
ingredients.notes: Toast or break into pieces to serve alongside.

ingredients.name: Green cooking banana
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly and soak in lightly acidulated water to limit browning.

preparation_steps.instruction: If frozen, thaw the sea-urchin meat in the refrigerator. Drain, check the smell and packaging, and keep chilled until mixing.
Wash and drain the greens; slice the green banana and soak it briefly in lightly acidulated water to limit browning.
Finely chop the scallions and crack the pepper. Prepare the rice cracker and a clean plate for the cooked patties.

cooking_steps.instruction: Put the sea-urchin meat in a bowl, gently break it up with a spoon, then beat with the scallions, fish sauce and pepper until combined. Keep cold if not frying immediately.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat. Spoon in small portions and flatten to about 1 cm thick; fry for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and the center reaches at least 63°C.
Transfer the patties to a clean paper-lined plate. Serve hot with sesame rice cracker, fresh greens and green banana.

cha-nhum-phu-quoc.media_alt_text: Golden fried sea-urchin cakes served with sesame rice crackers, fresh greens and green banana.
